title: Tether

beats.what: Jim and Julie confront Boyd on his return; Julie accuses him of coming back with no answers and abandoning the family
Jim comforts Ellis over Fatima nearly losing herself; tells Ellis to be the piece of her this place cannot take away
Kristi patches up Jim's cracked ribs; Jim and Tabitha reunite after she emerges from the tunnels
Boyd breaks up a standoff between bus survivor Randall and Donna, re-establishing his authority the morning after
Jade and Kenny find a bus survivor pinned to a tree by an iron rod, still alive, left there by the creatures
Jade confronts Victor to get the journal back; Victor furiously reclaims his property and his room
Kristi and Marielle discover they are engaged to each other through the town's proxy system
Kristi tells Kelly the truth: the wound through her body is fatal and she will die

character_beats.beat: Wants to lead people and project competence; returns to find the community splintered and immediately has to perform authority he does not feel, telling the armed bus survivor the rule about guns while hiding the tremors in his hands
Wants to be a healer; faces the case she cannot fix and must tell Kelly plainly she is going to die. Later pulls back emotionally from Marielle, saying she needs time and people died last night
Wants Victor's knowledge of the symbol; violates Victor's space to get the journal, loses it when Victor returns, and still cannot get Victor to cooperate

key_lines.line: You said you were gonna find answers or find a way home!
key_lines.why: Julie's accusation lands the season's central broken promise: Boyd left and came back empty-handed

key_lines.line: You have to be that piece of her that this place can't take away.
key_lines.why: Jim's instruction to Ellis about Fatima; states the show's survival thesis about human attachment
Kelly's direct question to Kristi; the episode's emotional fulcrum, met with an honest yes
Kristi's one-word answer to Kelly; the medical truth stated without softening, establishing Kristi's character

open_loops: The creatures pinned Kelly to a tree and left her alive for hours: what purpose does that serve for them?
Victor refuses to explain the symbol even when Jade shows him the Polaroid of his younger self: what is he protecting?
Tabitha saw two children standing in the road staring at her: what were they and what do they signal?
The wires in the basement were not connected to anything yet the lights still worked: what powers the electricity in this place?
Elgin had a waking dream on the bus about the Brundles lake before he arrived: how did he know about a place he had never been?

payoffs.what: Tabitha's collapse underground in S02E01 resolves: she emerges and reunites with Jim at the clinic

contradiction.wants: to be present for Marielle and rebuild their relationship after the impossible reunion
contradiction.does: withdraws immediately when called to Kelly, and when Marielle reaches out in the room, Kristi says she needs time and leaves again, using medical duty as a shield against intimacy

tone_notes: Runtime 49.7 min, 813 cues, 85.8 words/min. Two major silences: 366-484s (the music passage between the Jim-Boyd confrontation and Kristi stitching Jim up, nearly 2 minutes with near-zero dialogue) and 1504-1573s (69 seconds around the Kelly scene, the weight of impending death lowering the room). Density spikes at minutes 10-11 (165-117, the armed standoff with Randall) and 31 (133, the Kelly-in-the-tree discovery). The episode runs nearly 4 minutes longer than S02E01 and E02, carrying more aftermath than event.
